security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel, if pmap code (e.g., pmap_enter, pmap_remove, pmap_protect in sys/riscv/riscv/pmap.c) clears, ignores, or unconditionally overwrites the PTE Y-field bits (yr, yw, yd, ys) during page table manipulation — for example, when recycling PTEs, constructing new mappings, or performing demotion/promotion of superpages — without preserving or explicitly initializing these 4 capability-flow-control bits, the kernel silently destroys the hardware-managed capability dirty/read tracking state required by Svyrg semantics.
security_spec.summary: PR #996 removes the sstatus enable bit that previously gated the PTE Y-field capability-flow-control behavior, making Svyrg semantics the architectural default — FreeBSD's pmap layer must unconditionally preserve and manage the 4-bit Y-field (yr/yw/yd/ys) in all RV64 PTE formats, and the kernel's exception handlers must always recognize capability-load-fault and capability-dirty-store-fault cause values regardless of sstatus configuration, or else capability revocation tracking state will be silently corrupted on context switch and page table updates.

findings.finding: pmap_enter() constructs new_l3 from scratch starting with only PTE_V | PTE_R | PTE_A, then layers on PTE_X/PTE_D/PTE_W/PTE_U/PPN/PTE_SW_WIRED/memattr/PTE_SW_MANAGED. No Svyrg Y-field bits (yr/yw/yd/ys) are included. If Svyrg were made default, every newly created mapping would silently zero the Y-field capability-flow-control bits, destroying hardware-managed capability dirty/read tracking.

pmap_enter_quick_locked() constructs newl3 from scratch with only PTE_V | PTE_R | memattr_phys, then optionally adds PTE_X/PTE_U/PTE_SW_MANAGED. No Svyrg Y-field bits are initialized or preserved. If Svyrg were the default, speculative mappings (e.g. from pmap_enter_quick) would silently strip Y-field capability state.

location.function_name: pmap_clear / pmap_load_clear (macros used by pmap_kremove, pmap_qremove, pmap_remove_l3)

findings.finding: pmap_clear(pte) writes 0 unconditionally (pmap_store(pte, 0)), and pmap_load_clear(pte) does an atomic_swap_64 with 0. These are used in pmap_kremove() line 1331, pmap_qremove() line 1432, pmap_remove_l3() line 2579, and pmap_enter() line 3396. If Svyrg is default, these operations destroy Y-field bits in the cleared PTE as a side effect of zeroing the entry. The hardware-managed capability dirty/read state is lost.

pmap_promote_l2() stores firstl3e directly as the L2 superpage PTE. firstl3e comes from the first L3 PTE of the backing PTP, which was constructed by pmap_enter() without Y-field bits. The promoted superpage PTE therefore also lacks Y-field bits. If Svyrg is default, all promoted 2MB superpages would lack valid Y-field capability-flow-control state.

During demotion, oldl2 is copied to newl3 template, and each L3 PTE gets newl3 + (i << PTE_PPN0_S). This preserves whatever bits (including potential Y-field bits) were in the original L2 superpage PTE. This path would correctly propagate Y-field state if it existed in the source mapping.

pmap_clear_bits() uses atomic_clear_64 which only clears specified bits (PTE_D | PTE_W). This is a targeted bitmask operation that does not disturb other PTE bits including any potential Y-field bits. Safe operation with respect to Svyrg state preservation.

PTE_PROMOTE mask (defined in pte.h:83) covers only V, RWX, D, G, U, SW_MANAGED, SW_WIRED. It does NOT include any Y-field bits (yr, yw, yd, ys). In pmap_promote_l2() line 3196, the comparison (l3e & PTE_PROMOTE) != (firstl3e & PTE_PROMOTE) would not detect mismatching Y-field bits across the 512 L3 PTEs being promoted. If some 4K pages had different Y-field state, the promotion would silently squash the discrepancy into the first page's Y-field value.

PTE_HI_MASK (0xFFC0000000000000ULL) masks bits 63:54, declared as 'reserved for future use'. PTE_TO_PHYS() at pmap.c:375 uses ~PTE_HI_MASK to extract the physical address, which implicitly preserves bits 53:10 (including potential Y-field bits in Svyrg-capable hardware). However, the comment and mask are stale: Svyrg Y-field bits would need to be in the reserved range or other currently-unused PTE bits. No explicit reservation exists for Svyrg space.
findings.snippet:
/* Bits 63 - 54 are reserved for future use. */
#define PTE_HI_MASK	0xFFC0000000000000ULL
